q: 妈妈昨天买___两斤苹果。
zh: 妈妈昨天买了两斤苹果。
py: mā ma zuó tiān mǎi le liǎng jīn píng guǒ
en: Mom bought two jin of apples yesterday.
why: One finished purchase with a counted object: 了 goes right after 买. 过 would mean 'have bought at some time', which does not fit a specific purchase yesterday.

q: 我今天早上喝___一杯牛奶。
zh: 我今天早上喝了一杯牛奶。
py: wǒ jīn tiān zǎo shang hē le yī bēi niú nǎi
en: I drank a glass of milk this morning.
why: A single finished drink with a counted object takes 了 straight after 喝. 着 shows an ongoing state, and 过 is about experience, not one specific morning.

q: 弟弟刚才吃___三个包子。
zh: 弟弟刚才吃了三个包子。
py: dì di gāng cái chī le sān ge bāo zi
en: My younger brother just ate three steamed buns.
why: 刚才 points to one completed event with a counted object, so 了 follows 吃. 过 (ever done) and 着 (ongoing) both clash with 'just now'.

q: 姐姐刚才在网上买___一条很漂亮的裙子。
zh: 姐姐刚才在网上买了一条很漂亮的裙子。
py: jiě jie gāng cái zài wǎng shàng mǎi le yī tiáo hěn piào liang de qún zi
en: My older sister just bought a very pretty skirt online.
why: 刚才 plus a counted object marks one finished purchase, so 了 sits right after 买, before 一条. 过 and 着 cannot report a single event that just happened.

q: 他在超市排___二十分钟的队才付钱。
zh: 他在超市排了二十分钟的队才付钱。
py: tā zài chāo shì pái le èr shí fēn zhōng de duì cái fù qián
en: He stood in line at the supermarket for twenty minutes before paying.
why: A completed stretch of time (二十分钟) after the verb needs 了 right after 排. 着 cannot be followed by a duration, and 过 would not say this one wait is over.

q: 爸爸昨晚给孩子们做___一桌好菜。
zh: 爸爸昨晚给孩子们做了一桌好菜。
py: bà ba zuó wǎn gěi hái zi men zuò le yī zhuō hǎo cài
en: Dad cooked a whole table of good food for the kids last night.
why: One finished act with a counted object (一桌) takes 了 after 做. 昨晚 names a specific time, so 过 (a general experience) is out.

q: 奶奶为了给孙子买生日礼物，走___整整一个小时才找到那家商店。
zh: 奶奶为了给孙子买生日礼物，走了整整一个小时才找到那家商店。
py: nǎi nai wèi le gěi sūn zi mǎi shēng rì lǐ wù zǒu le zhěng zhěng yī ge xiǎo shí cái zhǎo dào nà jiā shāng diàn
en: To buy a birthday present for her grandson, Grandma walked a full hour before she found that shop.
why: The walking is over and measured by a full hour, so 了 goes right after 走. 着 cannot take a duration, and 过 would not report this one trip.

zh: 我昨天买了两件衣服。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi le liǎng jiàn yī fu
en: I bought two pieces of clothing yesterday.
why: 了 attaches to the verb 买, before the number 两件. Putting it after 衣服 would leave the counted object hanging.

zh: 妈妈在菜市场买了一条大鱼。
py: mā ma zài cài shì chǎng mǎi le yī tiáo dà yú
en: Mom bought a big fish at the market.
why: The place phrase comes before the verb, and 了 stays glued to 买, ahead of the counted object 一条大鱼.

src_py: bà ba yào mǎi yī tái diàn shì
task: Say he already bought it yesterday.
zh: 爸爸昨天买了一台电视。
py: bà ba zuó tiān mǎi le yī tái diàn shì
en: Dad bought a TV yesterday.
why: 要 is a plan; to report the finished purchase, drop 要 and put 了 right after 买, before the counted object 一台电视.

s: 她在商店买着三双鞋。
s_py: tā zài shāng diàn mǎi zhe sān shuāng xié
zh: 她在商店买了三双鞋。
py: tā zài shāng diàn mǎi le sān shuāng xié
en: She bought three pairs of shoes at the shop.
why: 着 marks a continuing state and cannot report a finished purchase of a counted object. 了 is needed after 买.

s: 我昨天花了两百块钱买衣服。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān huā le liǎng bǎi kuài qián mǎi yī fu
zh: 我昨天花了两百块钱买衣服。
py: wǒ zuó tiān huā le liǎng bǎi kuài qián mǎi yī fu
en: I spent two hundred yuan on clothes yesterday.
why: This is correct: only 花, whose amount is counted, takes 了. The second verb 买 does not need its own 了, and adding one would be unnecessary.

q: 我儿子已经七岁___。
zh: 我儿子已经七岁了。
py: wǒ ér zi yǐ jīng qī suì le
en: My son is already seven.
why: An age said as news ('he has reached seven') ends with 了, and 已经 expects it. 着, 过 and 的 cannot mark this change of state.

q: 外面下雨___，快把衣服收进来。
zh: 外面下雨了，快把衣服收进来。
py: wài miàn xià yǔ le kuài bǎ yī fu shōu jìn lái
en: It's started raining outside, quick, bring the clothes in.
why: The rain is a new situation that calls for action, so the clause ends in 了. 下雨着 is not possible, and 过 would say it rained at some earlier time.

q: 饭做好___，大家快来吃。
zh: 饭做好了，大家快来吃。
py: fàn zuò hǎo le dà jiā kuài lái chī
en: The food is ready, everyone come and eat.
why: 'The meal is ready now' is a change of state, so 了 closes the clause. 着 and 的 cannot report that something has just become ready.

q: 我女儿会自己穿衣服___，早上不再需要妈妈帮忙。
zh: 我女儿会自己穿衣服了，早上不再需要妈妈帮忙。
py: wǒ nǚ ér huì zì jǐ chuān yī fu le zǎo shang bù zài xū yào mā ma bāng máng
en: My daughter can dress herself now, so in the morning she no longer needs Mom's help.
why: 会 plus 了 says a new ability, and 不再 in the next clause confirms the change. 过 and 着 cannot express 'can now'.

q: 超市快要关门___，我们得抓紧时间买东西。
zh: 超市快要关门了，我们得抓紧时间买东西。
py: chāo shì kuài yào guān mén le wǒ men děi zhuā jǐn shí jiān mǎi dōng xi
en: The supermarket is about to close, we have to hurry and shop.
why: 快要 … 了 is the frame for 'about to'; 了 is part of the pattern and cannot be swapped for 着, 的 or 过.

q: 妈妈的头发都白___，可她还是每天早起给我们做早饭。
zh: 妈妈的头发都白了，可她还是每天早起给我们做早饭。
py: mā ma de tóu fa dōu bái le kě tā hái shi měi tiān zǎo qǐ gěi wǒ men zuò zǎo fàn
en: Mom's hair has all gone white, yet she still gets up early every day to make us breakfast.
why: 白 here is a change ('has turned white'), so 了 ends the clause. The contrast with 还是 in the next clause is what makes the change visible.

q: 听说那家商店下个月就要搬走___，所以现在所有东西都打五折。
zh: 听说那家商店下个月就要搬走了，所以现在所有东西都打五折。
py: tīng shuō nà jiā shāng diàn xià ge yuè jiù yào bān zǒu le suǒ yǐ xiàn zài suǒ yǒu dōng xi dōu dǎ wǔ zhé
en: I hear that shop is moving out next month, so everything is half price now.
why: 就要 … 了 marks a coming change, and 了 is required even though the moving is in the future. 着 and 过 do not fit this frame.

zh: 我弟弟已经会游泳了。
py: wǒ dì di yǐ jīng huì yóu yǒng le
en: My little brother can swim now.
why: 已经 comes before 会, and the new ability is closed by 了 at the very end. Placing 了 after 会 would break the pattern.

zh: 我们的新房子快要装修好了。
py: wǒ men de xīn fáng zi kuài yào zhuāng xiū hǎo le
en: Our new house is almost finished being renovated.
why: 快要 goes before the verb phrase and 了 closes the whole sentence to say the change is about to happen.

src_py: wǒ ér zi bù huì qí zì xíng chē
task: Say he can ride a bike now.
zh: 我儿子会骑自行车了。
py: wǒ ér zi huì qí zì xíng chē le
en: My son can ride a bike now.
why: Drop 不 and end with 了 to turn 'cannot' into 'can now'. Without 了 it would be a plain statement of ability.

s: 我女儿现在已经八岁。
s_py: wǒ nǚ ér xiàn zài yǐ jīng bā suì
zh: 我女儿现在已经八岁了。
py: wǒ nǚ ér xiàn zài yǐ jīng bā suì le
en: My daughter is already eight now.
why: 现在已经 plus an age reports a change and needs final 了. Without it the sentence sounds cut off.

s: 爷爷的身体好多了。
s_py: yé ye de shēn tǐ hǎo duō le
zh: 爷爷的身体好多了。
py: yé ye de shēn tǐ hǎo duō le
en: Grandpa's health is much better now.
why: This is correct: 好多了 reports improvement, a change, so 了 belongs at the end. Dropping it would turn it into a flat description.

q: 我们以前在城东住___三年___，后来才搬到城西。
zh: 我们以前在城东住了三年，后来才搬到城西。
py: wǒ men yǐ qián zài chéng dōng zhù le sān nián hòu lái cái bān dào chéng xī
en: We used to live in the east of the city for three years, then moved to the west.
why: 以前 and 后来 close the period, so only the 了 after 住 is needed. A second 了 would say they still live there, which 后来才搬 contradicts.

q: 去年我在那家店工作___三个月___，后来换了工作。
zh: 去年我在那家店工作了三个月，后来换了工作。
py: qù nián wǒ zài nà jiā diàn gōng zuò le sān ge yuè hòu lái huàn le gōng zuò
en: Last year I worked at that shop for three months, then changed jobs.
why: The three months are over (去年, 后来), so one 了 after the verb is enough. A final 了 would claim the job is still going on.

q: 我已经学___两年中文___，还想继续学。
zh: 我已经学了两年中文了，还想继续学。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le hái xiǎng jì xù xué
en: I've been studying Chinese for two years already, and I want to keep going.
why: 'So far, and still going' takes two 了: one after 学, one at the end. 着 cannot sit before a duration.

q: 我们在这家商店已经逛___两个小时___，还没决定买什么。
zh: 我们在这家商店已经逛了两个小时了，还没决定买什么。
py: wǒ men zài zhè jiā shāng diàn yǐ jīng guàng le liǎng ge xiǎo shí le hái méi jué dìng mǎi shén me
en: We've already been walking around this shop for two hours and still haven't decided what to buy.
why: Two hours so far, still ongoing (还没决定): 了 after 逛 and 了 at the end. 着 cannot follow a verb before a time length.

q: 他今天已经喝___三杯咖啡___，不能再喝了。
zh: 他今天已经喝了三杯咖啡了，不能再喝了。
py: tā jīn tiān yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le bù néng zài hē le
en: He has already had three cups of coffee today, he can't have more.
why: 已经 with an amount 'so far' takes 了 after the verb and 了 at the end. 着 cannot appear before the counted object.

q: 前几年爸爸在外地打工，一共攒___二十万块钱___，后来才回家。
zh: 前几年爸爸在外地打工，一共攒了二十万块钱，后来才回家。
py: qián jǐ nián bà ba zài wài dì dǎ gōng yī gòng zǎn le èr shí wàn kuài qián hòu lái cái huí jiā
en: A few years ago Dad worked away from home and saved 200,000 yuan in total, and only then came home.
why: 前几年 and 后来 place the saving in a finished stretch, so only 了 after 攒. A final 了 would mean the total is still counting now.

zh: 我们已经等了半个小时了。
py: wǒ men yǐ jīng děng le bàn ge xiǎo shí le
en: We've already been waiting for half an hour.
why: 已经 precedes the verb, 了 follows 等, and a second 了 ends the sentence to say the waiting has lasted this long so far.

zh: 我弟弟已经看了三个小时电视了。
py: wǒ dì di yǐ jīng kàn le sān ge xiǎo shí diàn shì le
en: My little brother has already been watching TV for three hours.
why: The first 了 sits on 看 before the duration; the final 了 says it has reached this point and is ongoing.

src_py: mā ma zuò le liǎng ge xiǎo shí fàn
task: Say she has been cooking for two hours so far, with 已经.
zh: 妈妈已经做了两个小时饭了。
py: mā ma yǐ jīng zuò le liǎng ge xiǎo shí fàn le
en: Mom has already been cooking for two hours.
why: Adding 已经 and a final 了 turns a closed duration into 'two hours so far'. The first 了 stays after 做.

s: 他已经喝三杯了咖啡。
s_py: tā yǐ jīng hē sān bēi le kā fēi
zh: 他已经喝了三杯咖啡。
py: tā yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi
en: He has already had three cups of coffee.
why: 了 must stay right after the verb 喝. It cannot move behind the measure word and split 三杯 from 咖啡.

s: 我姐姐以前在商场工作了两年，后来开了自己的小店。
s_py: wǒ jiě jie yǐ qián zài shāng chǎng gōng zuò le liǎng nián hòu lái kāi le zì jǐ de xiǎo diàn
zh: 我姐姐以前在商场工作了两年，后来开了自己的小店。
py: wǒ jiě jie yǐ qián zài shāng chǎng gōng zuò le liǎng nián hòu lái kāi le zì jǐ de xiǎo diàn
en: My older sister worked in a mall for two years, then opened her own little shop.
why: This is correct with a single 了: 以前 and 后来 show the two years are over. A final 了 after 两年 would wrongly say she still works there.

q: 我们吃___饭就去逛街。
zh: 我们吃了饭就去逛街。
py: wǒ men chī le fàn jiù qù guàng jiē
en: We'll go shopping as soon as we've eaten.
why: In 'after A, then B', 了 goes right after the first verb. 吃着饭 would mean eating while doing something else, not finishing first.

q: 你换___鞋再进屋。
zh: 你换了鞋再进屋。
py: nǐ huàn le xié zài jìn wū
en: Change your shoes before you come in.
why: 换了鞋再进屋: 了 marks the first step as done before 再 starts the second. 换着鞋 cannot be a preceding step.

q: 我们买___东西再回家，好吗？
zh: 我们买了东西再回家，好吗？
py: wǒ men mǎi le dōng xi zài huí jiā hǎo ma
en: Shall we buy the things first and then go home?
why: The shopping must be finished before going home, so the first verb takes 了 even though this is a plan. 着 cannot mark a completed first step.

q: 你写___作业再看电视，不然妈妈要生气。
zh: 你写了作业再看电视，不然妈妈要生气。
py: nǐ xiě le zuò yè zài kàn diàn shì bù rán mā ma yào shēng qì
en: Finish your homework before watching TV, or Mom will get angry.
why: 再 introduces the second step only once the first is done, so 了 follows 写. This 了 is not past tense; it works for a future instruction.

q: 昨天弟弟吃___晚饭就出去玩儿了，作业也没写。
zh: 昨天弟弟吃了晚饭就出去玩儿了，作业也没写。
py: zuó tiān dì di chī le wǎn fàn jiù chū qù wán r le zuò yè yě méi xiě
en: Yesterday my brother went out to play as soon as he'd eaten dinner, and didn't do his homework.
why: The first step 吃晚饭 is finished before 就 starts the second, so 了 follows 吃. The second 了 closes the past sequence. 着 would mean eating and playing at once.

q: 我们先付___钱再让商店把沙发送到家里。
zh: 我们先付了钱再让商店把沙发送到家里。
py: wǒ men xiān fù le qián zài ràng shāng diàn bǎ shā fā sòng dào jiā lǐ
en: We'll pay first and then have the shop deliver the sofa to our house.
why: 先…再 marks two ordered steps; the first is complete when the second starts, so 了 goes right after 付, before 钱. 着 would make no sense here.

zh: 你洗了手再吃饭。
py: nǐ xǐ le shǒu zài chī fàn
en: Wash your hands before you eat.
why: 了 stays on the first verb 洗, before its object 手; 再 then introduces the second step 吃饭.

zh: 爸爸下了班就去接孩子。
py: bà ba xià le bān jiù qù jiē hái zi
en: Dad goes to pick up the kids right after work.
why: 下了班 comes first (了 before 班's end), and 就 links it straight to the next action. 了 cannot be moved after 班 to the end of 下班就去接孩子.

src_py: wǒ chī wán fàn rán hòu qù shāng diàn
task: Rewrite with 了 and 就.
zh: 我吃了饭就去商店。
py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù qù shāng diàn
en: I'll go to the shop as soon as I've eaten.
why: Replace 吃完 and 然后 with 吃了 … 就: 了 on the first verb, 就 before the second step.

s: 我吃饭就了去找你。
s_py: wǒ chī fàn jiù le qù zhǎo nǐ
zh: 我吃了饭就去找你。
py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù qù zhǎo nǐ
en: I'll come and find you as soon as I've eaten.
why: 了 belongs right after the first verb 吃. It cannot float after 就 in front of the second verb.

s: 明天你下了课就来我家吧。
s_py: míng tiān nǐ xià le kè jiù lái wǒ jiā ba
zh: 明天你下了课就来我家吧。
py: míng tiān nǐ xià le kè jiù lái wǒ jiā ba
en: Come to my place tomorrow as soon as class is over.
why: This is correct: 了 after 下 means 'once class is over' and works for the future too. 明天 does not forbid it.

q: 我每天早上都喝___牛奶。
zh: 我每天早上都喝牛奶。
py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shang dōu hē niú nǎi
en: I drink milk every morning.
why: 每天 makes this a routine, and routines take no 了. 了 would turn it into one finished event, and 过 would be 'have once drunk'.

q: 妈妈常常去市场买___菜。
zh: 妈妈常常去市场买菜。
py: mā ma cháng cháng qù shì chǎng mǎi cài
en: Mom often goes to the market to buy vegetables.
why: 常常 marks a repeated action, so no 了 after 买. 着 does not fit, and 了 would make it one completed trip.

q: 我小时候，奶奶总是给我买___糖。
zh: 我小时候，奶奶总是给我买糖。
py: wǒ xiǎo shí hou nǎi nai zǒng shì gěi wǒ mǎi táng
en: When I was little, Grandma always bought me sweets.
why: 总是 shows a repeated habit, so even in the past there is no 了. English past tense tempts 了, but 过 or 了 would turn it into one event.

q: 以前我们每个星期天都在家吃___饭，很热闹。
zh: 以前我们每个星期天都在家吃饭，很热闹。
py: yǐ qián wǒ men měi ge xīng qī tiān dōu zài jiā chī fàn hěn rè nao
en: We used to eat at home every Sunday, and it was lively.
why: 每个星期天都 describes a routine, so 了 is left out, even though it is in the past (以前). 过 would mean 'have eaten once'.

q: 他一般在网上买___衣服，很少去商店。
zh: 他一般在网上买衣服，很少去商店。
py: tā yī bān zài wǎng shàng mǎi yī fu hěn shǎo qù shāng diàn
en: He usually buys clothes online and rarely goes to shops.
why: 一般 marks a general habit, which takes no 了. 了 would present a single finished purchase, which clashes with 很少去商店.

q: 那时候我们家不富裕，爸爸每个周末都骑自行车去很远的市场买___便宜的菜。
zh: 那时候我们家不富裕，爸爸每个周末都骑自行车去很远的市场买便宜的菜。
py: nà shí hou wǒ men jiā bù fù yù bà ba měi ge zhōu mò dōu qí zì xíng chē qù hěn yuǎn de shì chǎng mǎi pián yi de cài
en: At that time our family was not well off; Dad rode his bike to a faraway market every weekend to buy cheap vegetables.
why: 每个周末都 turns the buying into a repeated habit in the past, so no 了 after 买. 买了便宜的菜 would be one specific trip.

zh: 小时候我每个星期都去奶奶家。
py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ měi ge xīng qī dōu qù nǎi nai jiā
en: When I was little I went to Grandma's house every week.
why: 每个星期都 marks a habit, so the verb 去 takes no 了 despite the past time frame. The time word 小时候 can come before or after 我.

src_py: wǒ zuó tiān qù chāo shì le
task: Say you go to the supermarket every Saturday.
zh: 我每个星期六都去超市。
py: wǒ měi ge xīng qī liù dōu qù chāo shì
en: I go to the supermarket every Saturday.
why: Changing a one-time event to a routine removes 了 and brings in 每…都. A habit is not a completed event.

s: 小时候我常常去了奶奶家。
s_py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ cháng cháng qù le nǎi nai jiā
zh: 小时候我常常去奶奶家。
py: xiǎo shí hou wǒ cháng cháng qù nǎi nai jiā
en: When I was little I often went to Grandma's house.
why: 常常 shows a repeated habit, which never takes 了 after the verb. English past tense does not call for 了 here.

s: 爸爸现在每天自己做饭了。
s_py: bà ba xiàn zài měi tiān zì jǐ zuò fàn le
zh: 爸爸现在每天自己做饭了。
py: bà ba xiàn zài měi tiān zì jǐ zuò fàn le
en: Dad cooks for himself every day now.
why: This is correct: the final 了 does not mark a finished event but a new habit (he did not use to). That is the change-of-state 了.

q: 我昨天___买那件外套，太贵了。
zh: 我昨天没买那件外套，太贵了。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi mǎi nà jiàn wài tào tài guì le
en: I didn't buy that coat yesterday, it was too expensive.
why: 'Did not do it' in the past is 没 + verb. 不 describes a decision or habit, and 别 is a command.

q: 妈妈今天早上没做饭___，我们在外面吃的。
zh: 妈妈今天早上没做饭，我们在外面吃的。
py: mā ma jīn tiān zǎo shang méi zuò fàn wǒ men zài wài miàn chī de
en: Mom didn't cook this morning; we ate out.
why: 没 already says it did not happen, so no 了 follows. 没做饭了 would mean she doesn't cook any more, and 没做过 would mean never.

q: 爸爸昨天没给我买___那个玩具，我有点儿不高兴。
zh: 爸爸昨天没给我买那个玩具，我有点儿不高兴。
py: bà ba zuó tiān méi gěi wǒ mǎi nà ge wán jù wǒ yǒu diǎn r bù gāo xìng
en: Dad didn't buy me that toy yesterday, so I was a bit unhappy.
why: 没 + verb negates a specific event and cannot carry 了. 没买过 would mean 'has never bought', which does not fit 昨天.

q: 他们上个周末___去逛街，因为下大雨。
zh: 他们上个周末没去逛街，因为下大雨。
py: tā men shàng ge zhōu mò méi qù guàng jiē yīn wèi xià dà yǔ
en: They didn't go shopping last weekend because it rained heavily.
why: Last weekend is past, and 'did not go' is 没去. 不去 would be a refusal or habit, and 要去 is future.

q: 我出门时一分钱都没带___，只好回家拿。
zh: 我出门时一分钱都没带，只好回家拿。
py: wǒ chū mén shí yī fēn qián dōu méi dài zhǐ hǎo huí jiā ná
en: I didn't bring a single cent when I went out, so I had to go home and get it.
why: 没带 says the bringing did not happen; 了 cannot be added. 没带过 would mean 'never brought', which clashes with 出门时.

q: 因为那家商店的东西太贵，所以我们昨天什么也没买___，直接回家了。
zh: 因为那家商店的东西太贵，所以我们昨天什么也没买，直接回家了。
py: yīn wèi nà jiā shāng diàn de dōng xi tài guì suǒ yǐ wǒ men zuó tiān shén me yě méi mǎi zhí jiē huí jiā le
en: Because things were too expensive in that shop, we bought nothing yesterday and went straight home.
why: 什么也没买 is a plain negative of a past event, so no 了 follows 买. 了 belongs only at the end of the second clause, 回家了.

zh: 我还没吃早饭。
py: wǒ hái méi chī zǎo fàn
en: I haven't had breakfast yet.
why: 还没 + verb says it has not happened yet, with no 了. The object 早饭 can also be fronted as a topic.

src_py: wǒ mǎi le nà jiàn yī fu
zh: 我没买那件衣服。
py: wǒ méi mǎi nà jiàn yī fu
en: I didn't buy that dress.
why: Negating a completed action uses 没 and removes 了. 不买了 would mean a change of mind, not that it did not happen.

src_py: dì di zuó tiān xǐ le wǎn
zh: 弟弟昨天没洗碗。
py: dì di zuó tiān méi xǐ wǎn
en: My brother didn't wash the dishes yesterday.
why: 没 goes before the verb and 了 is dropped. Keeping 了 (没洗了碗) is the classic mistake.

s: 我昨天没去了商店。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù le shāng diàn
zh: 我昨天没去商店。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù shāng diàn
en: I didn't go to the shop yesterday.
why: 没 already negates the completed action, so 了 cannot follow the verb. 没去了 is not a Chinese pattern.

s: 我们家已经三天没吃米饭了。
s_py: wǒ men jiā yǐ jīng sān tiān méi chī mǐ fàn le
zh: 我们家已经三天没吃米饭了。
py: wǒ men jiā yǐ jīng sān tiān méi chī mǐ fàn le
en: Our family hasn't eaten rice for three days now.
why: This is correct: 'time + 没 + verb + 了' is a fixed pattern for how long something has not happened. 了 here marks the length so far, not a completed act.

q: 昨天是妈妈的生日___，我们一起吃了蛋糕。
zh: 昨天是妈妈的生日，我们一起吃了蛋糕。
py: zuó tiān shì mā ma de shēng rì wǒ men yī qǐ chī le dàn gāo
en: Yesterday was Mom's birthday, and we ate cake together.
why: 是 describes what the day was, a state, so there is no 了; 昨天 already shows it is past. 了 is correctly used in the second clause (吃了蛋糕).

q: 我小时候很喜欢___奶奶做的面条。
zh: 我小时候很喜欢奶奶做的面条。
py: wǒ xiǎo shí hou hěn xǐ huan nǎi nai zuò de miàn tiáo
en: When I was little I really liked the noodles Grandma made.
why: 喜欢 is a state of mind, not an event, so no 了. 小时候 supplies the past; 喜欢了 would mean 'came to like'.

q: 昨天商场里人很多___，我们没买到想买的东西。
zh: 昨天商场里人很多，我们没买到想买的东西。
py: zuó tiān shāng chǎng lǐ rén hěn duō wǒ men méi mǎi dào xiǎng mǎi de dōng xi
en: There were lots of people in the mall yesterday, so we couldn't buy what we wanted.
why: A description with 很 + adjective takes no 了, even in the past. 昨天 shows the time. 了 would imply a change in the crowd, which makes no sense here.

q: 我觉得___那个沙发很舒服，所以买下来了。
zh: 我觉得那个沙发很舒服，所以买下来了。
py: wǒ jué de nà ge shā fā hěn shū fu suǒ yǐ mǎi xià lái le
en: I thought that sofa was very comfortable, so I bought it.
why: 觉得 is a state of mind, never followed by 了 to mean 'thought'. The 了 belongs to 买下来, the real event.

q: 上个月这家商店有___很多便宜的东西，现在都卖完了。
zh: 上个月这家商店有很多便宜的东西，现在都卖完了。
py: shàng ge yuè zhè jiā shāng diàn yǒu hěn duō pián yi de dōng xi xiàn zài dōu mài wán le
en: Last month this shop had lots of cheap things; now they are all sold out.
why: 有 describes what the shop had, a state, so no 了. 有了 would mean 'came to have'. 了 is right in 卖完了, which is a real event.

q: 那时候这条街上最大的那家商店是___我舅舅开的，所以我们买东西很便宜。
zh: 那时候这条街上最大的那家商店是我舅舅开的，所以我们买东西很便宜。
py: nà shí hou zhè tiáo jiē shàng zuì dà de nà jiā shāng diàn shì wǒ jiù jiu kāi de suǒ yǐ wǒ men mǎi dōng xi hěn pián yi
en: At that time the biggest shop on this street was run by my uncle, so shopping there was cheap for us.
why: 是 only links two things and takes no 了, even about the past; 那时候 gives the time. 是了 does not mean 'was'.

zh: 姐姐小时候很喜欢吃糖。
py: jiě jie xiǎo shí hou hěn xǐ huan chī táng
en: My older sister really liked eating sweets when she was little.
why: A past liking is a state, so the sentence carries no 了; 小时候 shows the time. The time word may come before or after 姐姐.

src_py: wǒ gē ge xiàn zài shì lǎo shī
task: Say he was a teacher last year.
zh: 我哥哥去年是老师。
py: wǒ gē ge qù nián shì lǎo shī
en: My older brother was a teacher last year.
why: Moving to the past only changes the time word. 是 stays bare, with no 了, because it states what someone was.

s: 他去年是了我们的邻居。
s_py: tā qù nián shì le wǒ men de lín jū
zh: 他去年是我们的邻居。
py: tā qù nián shì wǒ men de lín jū
en: He was our neighbor last year.
why: 是 never takes 了 to mean 'was'; the time word 去年 already places it in the past.

s: 我觉得了这件衣服很便宜。
s_py: wǒ jué de le zhè jiàn yī fu hěn pián yi
zh: 我觉得这件衣服很便宜。
py: wǒ jué de zhè jiàn yī fu hěn pián yi
en: I thought this piece of clothing was cheap.
why: 觉得 expresses a view, not a finished act, so it cannot take 了. Past 'thought' is simply 觉得.

s: 天冷了，我们给孩子买了一件厚外套。
s_py: tiān lěng le wǒ men gěi hái zi mǎi le yī jiàn hòu wài tào
zh: 天冷了，我们给孩子买了一件厚外套。
py: tiān lěng le wǒ men gěi hái zi mǎi le yī jiàn hòu wài tào
en: It's got cold, so we bought the child a thick coat.
why: This is correct: 冷了 reports a new situation, and 买了一件 is a finished, counted action. A bare 冷 would be a plain description.

q: 这双鞋太贵___，我不买。
zh: 这双鞋太贵了，我不买。
py: zhè shuāng xié tài guì le wǒ bù mǎi
en: These shoes are too expensive, I won't buy them.
why: A complete remark with 太 + adjective closes with 了. 过, 着 and 的 cannot end this pattern.

q: 哇，这个蛋糕太好吃___！
zh: 哇，这个蛋糕太好吃了！
py: wā zhè ge dàn gāo tài hǎo chī le
en: Wow, this cake is so delicious!
why: 太…了 is the frame for an exclamation. The remark ends on the adjective, and 了 is part of the frame, not a past marker.

q: 这个书包___好看了，我真想买下来。
zh: 这个书包太好看了，我真想买下来。
py: zhè ge shū bāo tài hǎo kàn le wǒ zhēn xiǎng mǎi xià lái
en: This bag is so nice, I really want to buy it.
why: 太…了 frames the exclamation. 非常 does not take 了, and 不太 would say 'not very', which clashes with 真想买.

q: 孩子说今天的作业___多了，写不完。
zh: 孩子说今天的作业太多了，写不完。
py: hái zi shuō jīn tiān de zuò yè tài duō le xiě bù wán
en: The child says there's too much homework today and he can't finish it.
why: 太 + adjective + 了 means 'too much', which explains 写不完. 非常 does not go with 了, and 不太 would say there isn't much.

q: 这个房子又大又干净，我们___喜欢了。
zh: 这个房子又大又干净，我们太喜欢了。
py: zhè ge fáng zi yòu dà yòu gān jìng wǒ men tài xǐ huan le
en: This house is big and clean, we like it so much.
why: 太…了 can also wrap a verb like 喜欢 for 'so much'. 非常 would not take 了, and 不太 says 'not very', which contradicts the praise.

q: 听说那家超市今天所有水果都打三折，这也太便宜___！
zh: 听说那家超市今天所有水果都打三折，这也太便宜了！
py: tīng shuō nà jiā chāo shì jīn tiān suǒ yǒu shuǐ guǒ dōu dǎ sān zhé zhè yě tài pián yi le
en: I hear all the fruit at that supermarket is 70% off today, that's so cheap!
why: The remark ends on the adjective, so it closes with 了 as part of 太…了. 着 and 过 cannot end an exclamation like this.

zh: 这件衣服太贵了。
py: zhè jiàn yī fu tài guì le
en: This piece of clothing is too expensive.
why: 太 comes before the adjective and the remark ends with 了. 了 cannot go before 贵.

zh: 你买的这张桌子太大了。
py: nǐ mǎi de zhè zhāng zhuō zi tài dà le
en: The table you bought is too big.
why: The long subject 你买的这张桌子 comes first, then 太 + adjective, closed by 了.

src_py: zhè ge fáng jiān hěn dà
task: Say it is too big, with 太.
zh: 这个房间太大了。
py: zhè ge fáng jiān tài dà le
en: This room is too big.
why: Replace 很 with 太 and add 了 at the end. 很 takes no 了 but 太 needs it.

s: 这个包太了贵。
s_py: zhè ge bāo tài le guì
zh: 这个包太贵了。
py: zhè ge bāo tài guì le
en: This bag is too expensive.
why: In 太…了, 了 comes after the adjective, not before it. 太了贵 is not a possible order.

s: 今天不太冷，你不用穿那么多。
s_py: jīn tiān bù tài lěng nǐ bù yòng chuān nà me duō
zh: 今天不太冷，你不用穿那么多。
py: jīn tiān bù tài lěng nǐ bù yòng chuān nà me duō
en: It isn't very cold today, you don't need to wear so much.
why: This is correct: 不太 means 'not very' and does not take 了. The final 了 is only for the 太…了 exclamation.

s: 孩子们太高兴了，一直跳来跳去。
s_py: hái zi men tài gāo xìng le yī zhí tiào lái tiào qù
zh: 孩子们太高兴了，一直跳来跳去。
py: hái zi men tài gāo xìng le yī zhí tiào lái tiào qù
en: The kids were so happy they kept jumping about.
why: This is correct: 太…了 works for a past scene too. It does not need a time word, and it is not the 'finished event' 了.

q: 我不喝可乐___，我现在喝水。
zh: 我不喝可乐了，我现在喝水。
py: wǒ bù hē kě lè le wǒ xiàn zài hē shuǐ
en: I don't drink cola any more; now I drink water.
why: 'Not any more' is 不 + verb + 了. The next clause (现在喝水) shows the change; 着, 过 and 的 cannot express it.

q: 钱不够，我们不买那台电视___。
zh: 钱不够，我们不买那台电视了。
py: qián bú gòu wǒ men bù mǎi nà tái diàn shì le
en: There isn't enough money, so we won't buy that TV after all.
why: 不买…了 means a changed plan ('after all'). 了 must come at the end of the sentence.

q: 妈妈说家里没有米___，让我下班去超市买。
zh: 妈妈说家里没有米了，让我下班去超市买。
py: mā ma shuō jiā lǐ méi yǒu mǐ le ràng wǒ xià bān qù chāo shì mǎi
en: Mom says we're out of rice at home and asked me to buy some at the supermarket after work.
why: 没有 + noun + 了 means 'none left'. 了 closes the clause; 过 would mean 'never had', which is not the point.

q: 本来说好今天一起去商场，可是下雨了，我们___去了。
zh: 本来说好今天一起去商场，可是下雨了，我们不去了。
py: běn lái shuō hǎo jīn tiān yī qǐ qù shāng chǎng kě shì xià yǔ le wǒ men bù qù le
en: We had agreed to go to the mall together today, but it rained, so we're not going after all.
why: A changed plan is 不 + verb + 了. 没去 reports that it did not happen, and 没去了 is not a valid pattern.

q: 爸爸以前每天抽一包烟，自从生病以后，他再也不抽烟___。
zh: 爸爸以前每天抽一包烟，自从生病以后，他再也不抽烟了。
py: bà ba yǐ qián měi tiān chōu yī bāo yān zì cóng shēng bìng yǐ hòu tā zài yě bù chōu yān le
en: Dad used to smoke a pack a day, but since he got ill he doesn't smoke at all any more.
why: 再也不…了 means 'never again'. 了 ends the sentence to mark the change from before. 过 and 着 cannot do that.

zh: 弟弟不吃糖了。
py: dì di bù chī táng le
en: My little brother doesn't eat sweets any more.
why: 不 + verb goes before the object, and 了 ends the sentence to say the situation has changed.

zh: 我们家这个月已经没有钱了。
py: wǒ men jiā zhè ge yuè yǐ jīng méi yǒu qián le
en: Our family has no money left this month.
why: 没有 + noun + 了 says 'none left' and 了 comes last. 已经 sits before 没有.

src_py: dì di xǐ huan zhè ge wán jù
task: Say he doesn't like it any more.
zh: 弟弟不喜欢这个玩具了。
py: dì di bù xǐ huan zhè ge wán jù le
en: My brother doesn't like this toy any more.
why: Negate with 不 and add 了 at the end to mean 'not any more'. 没喜欢 is not possible.

s: 他不去了商场。
s_py: tā bù qù le shāng chǎng
zh: 他不去商场了。
py: tā bù qù shāng chǎng le
en: He doesn't go to the mall any more.
why: In 不…了, the 了 goes at the end of the sentence, after the object. 了 cannot sit right after 去.

s: 孩子大了，妈妈不用天天给他买衣服了。
s_py: hái zi dà le mā ma bù yòng tiān tiān gěi tā mǎi yī fu le
zh: 孩子大了，妈妈不用天天给他买衣服了。
py: hái zi dà le mā ma bù yòng tiān tiān gěi tā mǎi yī fu le
en: The child has grown up, so Mom doesn't have to buy him clothes every day any more.
why: This is correct: two sentence-final 了, one for 大了 (change) and one for 不用…了 ('no longer need'). Both mark a changed situation.
